course.title: Artificial Intelligence
course.description: This course introduces core concepts and techniques in Artificial Intelligence, including search, reasoning, learning, and planning. Students explore both classical and modern AI approaches through project-based learning, applying tools like Python to real-world problems. Emphasis is placed on ethical awareness, collaboration, and critical thinking. By course end, students will be able to design intelligent systems and evaluate their societal impact within Cambodia’s digital transformation context.

contentRows: Topic 1: What is Artificial Intelligence? Definition, goals, and scope of AI

topics.title: Topic 1: What is Artificial Intelligence? Definition, goals, and scope of AI
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe key definitions, goals, and historical milestones of AI. LLO2: Differentiate symbolic, statistical, and hybrid approaches in AI systems. LLO3: Identify real-world applications demonstrating the scope of AI across industries.

topics.title: Topic 2: Agent Architectures and Hierarchical Control: Designing intelligent agents and modular control systems
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the structure and behavior of intelligent agents in various environments. LLO2: Compare different agent architectures (reactive, deliberative, hybrid). LLO3: Construct simple agent control flows demonstrating modular or hierarchical decision-making.

topics.title: Topic 3: Searching for Solutions: State-space search, uninformed and informed search strategies
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe the components of state-space problem formulation. LLO2: Apply uninformed and informed search algorithms to solve structured problems. LLO3: Evaluate the completeness, optimality, and complexity of different search strategies.

topics.title: Topic 4: Reasoning with Constraints: Constraint satisfaction problems and optimization
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Define constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) and their core components. LLO2: Apply backtracking and heuristic-based methods to solve CSPs. LLO3: Analyze CSP solution performance in terms of consistency and constraint propagation.

topics.title: Topic 5: Propositional Logic and Inference: Logical reasoning and knowledge representation
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Represent knowledge using propositional logic expressions and formulas. LLO2: Apply inference rules such as resolution for logical deduction. LLO3: Evaluate the soundness and completeness of propositional reasoning methods.

topics.title: Topic 6: Deterministic Planning: Planning actions in fully observable, deterministic environments
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe the fundamentals of deterministic planning in AI environments. LLO2: Construct planning problems using formalisms such as STRIPS or state-transition graphs. LLO3: Compare forward, backward, and heuristic-based planning approaches.

topics.title: Topic 7: Supervised Machine Learning: Learning from labeled data, decision trees, regression
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the principles of supervised learning and its use cases. LLO2: Implement decision tree and regression models using Python libraries. LLO3: Assess model performance using standard evaluation metrics.

topics.title: Topic 8: Neural Networks and Deep Learning: Feedforward networks, CNNs, RNNs, transformers
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe the architecture and functioning of feedforward, convolutional, and recurrent networks. LLO2: Construct simple neural network models using deep learning frameworks. LLO3: Evaluate model performance and behavior under different hyperparameter settings.

topics.title: Topic 9: Reasoning with Uncertainty: Probability, belief networks, and probabilistic inference
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain foundational probability concepts relevant to intelligent systems. LLO2: Construct belief networks to represent uncertain relationships between variables. LLO3: Apply probabilistic inference algorithms to compute beliefs or likelihoods.

topics.title: Topic 10: Learning with Uncertainty: Bayesian learning, unsupervised learning, belief networks
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe Bayesian learning and unsupervised learning principles. LLO2: Implement basic Bayesian or unsupervised models using Python libraries. LLO3: Compare learning outcomes under different uncertainty assumptions.

topics.title: Topic 11: Causality in AI: Causal models, do-calculus, counterfactual reasoning
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain causal graphs and key ideas in causal modeling. LLO2: Apply do-calculus concepts to reason about interventions. LLO3: Analyze the difference between correlation, causation, and counterfactual reasoning.

topics.title: Topic 12: Reinforcement Learning: Learning through interaction and reward signals
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe reinforcement learning components: states, actions, rewards, and policies. LLO2: Implement basic RL algorithms such as Q-learning or policy iteration. LLO3: Evaluate agent performance under different reward structures or learning settings.

topics.title: Topic 13: Multiagent Systems: Game theory, Nash equilibria, cooperation and competition
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain key concepts in multiagent environments, including cooperation and competition. LLO2: Apply foundational game theory concepts such as Nash equilibria. LLO3: Analyze multiagent interactions and strategies in simulated environments.

topics.title: Topic 14: Social Impact of Artificial Intelligence: Ethics, bias, sustainability, governance
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify major ethical issues in AI, including bias, transparency, and fairness. LLO2: Explain sustainability, governance, and policy considerations related to AI deployment. LLO3: Evaluate the societal impacts of AI systems through real-world case studies.

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 1: What is Artificial Intelligence? Definition, goals, and scope of AI
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Interactive lecture explaining AI definitions, history, and milestones LLO2: Instructor compares symbolic, statistical, and hybrid AI approaches LLO3: Case‑based presentation of real-world AI applications
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students create a mind map summarizing AI goals and history LLO2: Students categorize AI examples into symbolic/statistical/hybrid LLO3: Students analyze an AI application and share findings in pairs

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 2: Agent Architectures and Hierarchical Control: Designing intelligent agents and modular control systems
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Diagram-based explanation of agent structures and environments LLO2: Instructor-led comparison of reactive, deliberative, and hybrid agents LLO3: Coding demonstration of a simple hierarchical agent
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students draw an agent–environment interaction diagram LLO2: Students complete a comparison worksheet on agent types LLO3: Students build a simple rule-based agent in Python

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 3: Searching for Solutions: State-space search, uninformed and informed search strategies
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture on components of state-space search LLO2: Demonstration of BFS, DFS, and A* LLO3: Instructor-led comparison of completeness, optimality, and complexity
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students write a state‑space model for a toy problem LLO2: Students implement BFS/A* during lab LLO3: Students compare BFS vs. A* using a structured table

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 4: Reasoning with Constraints: Constraint satisfaction problems and optimization
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture introducing CSP vocabulary and examples LLO2: Instructor demonstration of solving CSPs with backtracking LLO3: Explanation of heuristics like MRV and forward-checking
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students define variables, domains, constraints for a CSP LLO2: Students code a simple backtracking solver LLO3: Students experiment with heuristics and record performance differences

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 5: Propositional Logic and Inference: Logical reasoning and knowledge representation
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture illustrating propositional representation with examples LLO2: Step-by-step demonstration of inference using resolution LLO3: Instructor explains soundness and completeness concepts
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students convert natural language to propositional formulas LLO2: Students solve inference problems on worksheets LLO3: Students analyze inference outcomes and justify correctness

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 6: Deterministic Planning: Planning actions in fully observable, deterministic environments
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture explaining STRIPS and deterministic planning LLO2: Instructor builds a planning graph live LLO3: Guided comparison of forward, backward, heuristic planners
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students identify preconditions and effects for actions LLO2: Students create a STRIPS‑formatted planning problem LLO3: Students evaluate planning strategies for different scenarios

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 7: Supervised Machine Learning: Learning from labeled data, decision trees, regression
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture introducing supervised learning pipeline and examples LLO2: Coding demo of regression and decision trees LLO3: Explanation of performance metrics (accuracy, MSE)
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students classify ML tasks (classification vs regression) LLO2: Students train ML models using scikit‑learn LLO3: Students compute evaluation metrics for model performance

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 8: Neural Networks and Deep Learning: Feedforward networks, CNNs, RNNs, transformers
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Diagram-based lecture on CNNs, RNNs, feedforward networks LLO2: Coding demo building a simple NN LLO3: Instructor compares training outcomes under different hyperparameters
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students annotate diagrams to show information flow LLO2: Students implement a small neural network model LLO3: Students run experiments and compare accuracy results

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 9: Reasoning with Uncertainty: Probability, belief networks, and probabilistic inference
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture on basic probability concepts LLO2: Instructor constructs a belief network example step-by-step LLO3: Demonstration of probabilistic inference calculations
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students solve probability exercises LLO2: Students construct a belief network for a given scenario LLO3: Students compute posterior probabilities manually or via Python

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 10: Learning with Uncertainty: Bayesian learning, unsupervised learning, belief networks
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture on Bayesian learning and unsupervised methods LLO2: Coding demonstration (Naive Bayes, K-means) LLO3: Explanation of influence of priors and assumptions
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students categorize examples into Bayesian/unsupervised LLO2: Students implement Naive Bayes or K-means LLO3: Students compare model performance under different assumptions

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 11: Causality in AI: Causal models, do-calculus, counterfactual reasoning
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture on causal models and DAGs LLO2: Instructor-led examples applying do‑calculus LLO3: Case study highlighting correlation vs. causation issues
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students draw causal DAGs for sample problems LLO2: Students compute do‑intervention values LLO3: Students critique misleading correlations from examples

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 12: Reinforcement Learning: Learning through interaction and reward signals
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture explaining RL components and MDP structure LLO2: Coding demo of Q-learning LLO3: Demonstration of agent performance curves
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students identify states/actions/rewards in RL tasks LLO2: Students implement Q-learning in Python LLO3: Students analyze agent performance under different rewards

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 13: Multiagent Systems: Game theory, Nash equilibria, cooperation and competition
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture on cooperation, competition, communication LLO2: Instructor solves game-theoretic problems (payoff matrices) LLO3: Demonstration of multiagent simulation
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students identify multiagent interaction patterns LLO2: Students compute Nash equilibria LLO3: Students run a multiagent simulation and analyze behavior

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 14: Social Impact of Artificial Intelligence: Ethics, bias, sustainability, governance
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture on ethics, fairness, bias LLO2: Case-based discussion on governance frameworks LLO3: Instructor-led discussion on societal impacts
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students evaluate an AI ethics case study LLO2: Students summarize governance and policy frameworks LLO3: Students write a short reflection on the impact of AI on society

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
